intended_object: The factorization (corestriction) of a functor F : C ⥤ Comma L R through the non-full subcategory P.Comma L R Q W of the comma category. That subcategory has as objects those whose structure morphism satisfies P, and as morphisms those whose left and right components satisfy Q and W. This is read off the docstring and the module.
explanation:
This is the standard universal property of a subcategory: a functor lands in the subcategory exactly when every object it hits satisfies P and every morphism it hits has left component in Q and right component in W. In that case it factors uniquely through the inclusion.

The body does exactly this. On objects it keeps the underlying comma object of F.obj X and attaches the proof hP X. On morphisms it keeps the underlying comma morphism F.map f and attaches the proofs hQ f and hW f. The functor laws hold automatically because composition and identities in P.Comma are those of Comma L R.

The setting is fully general: arbitrary categories A, B, T and C, and arbitrary functors L and R. The only assumptions on Q and W are that they are multiplicative, which is what makes P.Comma L R Q W a category at all.

Mathlib has no other declaration for this specific lift; the analogous constructions for other kinds of subcategories (such as full subcategories) are separate.
